newsitem.title: UK: Brown says UK budget will be for long term.
newsitem.headline: Brown says UK budget will be for long term.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said his first budget on Wednesday would be a budget for the long term.
"Tomorrow's will be a budget for the long term. It will equip the country for the future and will meet the people's priorities," he said at a photocall to launch a new guide to the budget.
The Chancellor will start delivering the first budget by a Labour government since 1978 at 1430 GMT on Wednesday.
The centrepiece of the budget will be a "welfare-to-work" programme to create jobs for 250,000 young people, which will be financed by a "windfall" levy on the profits of privatised utilities.
Many economists also expect him to raise other taxes on the corporate sector and to impose some fiscal tightening on the personal sector to rein in soaring consumer demand.
Brown was announcing a new way for people to have free access to information on the budget by requesting a pocket guide to the budget through a Freepost service.
"I want to be more open with the British people. I want them to understand more about the way in which they are taxed and how the money is spent," Brown said.
"Just as there should be no taxation without representation, there should be no taxation without information."
